The normalized potentials tend uniformly to zero, while their normalized logarithmic densities are pairwise distinct, uniformly C0 bounded, unbounded in C1 and not equicontinuous. Both exact-adjoint densities still satisfy the663 uniform bounds. Two complete final manual reads,20 mathematical obligations and3 supplementary chain-rule identities pass. manual_mathematical_obligations.check: The construction uses the same fixed compact complex manifold, Hermitian background, probability volume and epsilon as663, including zero lower mass.
A compactly supported smooth cutoff equal to1 near the chart origin makes each global oscillation smooth after zero extension.
For x=Re z1, dc x=dy1/(4pi), so beta=dx wedge dcx=ddc(x^2/2)=i dz1 wedge dbarz1/(8pi).
Beta is nonzero semipositive of rank1 and beta^2=0.
ddc(sin(jx)/j^2)=-sin(jx) beta because ddc x=0.
The product rule has the two mixed terms a cos(jx)/j times(dzeta wedge dcx+dx wedge dczeta), plus a sin(jx) ddc zeta/j^2.
Each fixed form times its cutoff derivative has compact support, so a single C bounds the omega-operator norm by aC for all j>=1.
A fixed positive a with aC<=epsilon/2 puts every potential in the full controlled-Hessian family.
Subtracting sup wj changes no complex Hessian and gives sup vj=0 and C0 norm<=2a/j^2.
Omega_j is uniformly positive; its normalized density is defined by the actual solution form, not by an unproved existence estimate for prescribed densities.
At the common origin sin0=0 and the cutoff is constant, so Omega_j(p)=omega(p).
Differentiating the coordinate form at p gives partial_x Omega_j=partial_x omega-aj beta.
The number c_j is constant in spatial x, hence disappears from partial_x F_j.
Log-determinant differentiation gives partial_x F_j(p)=partial_x log(omega^n/dV)(p)-aj s, with s=tr_omega(p) beta>0.
The nonzero fixed slope proves pairwise distinction and unbounded C1 norms, without incorrectly inferring equicontinuity failure from C1 growth alone.
The existing663 theorem gives a uniform C0 bound for all normalized F_j.
Both points with x=+/-pi/(2j), other real coordinates0, lie in the constant-cutoff region for large j.
The limiting forms omega(p)+/-a beta have volumes(1+/-as)omega(p)^n; the uniform comparison ensures as<1.
The normalized-log-density difference cancels c_j and tends to log((1+as)/(1-as))>0 while the point distance tends to0.
Only exact maximizers for this controlled-form sequence receive the663 bounds; no assertion about all tests, arbitrary continuous data, P16 or uniqueness of weak limits is made.
